criteria.notes: CORRECTED by the pre-merge squad, evidence lens. The previous entry closed this at a4facaa2 and was five commits stale across two commits that added wait durations, one of them a 20000ms literal disclosed nowhere. That literal has since been REPLACED with 10000ms so the helper's worst case stays well inside Playwright's default 30000ms per-test timeout, preserving the self-describing failure message instead of a bare 'Test timeout exceeded'. A new wait budget is classified as a DISCLOSURE rather than a suppression on purpose: counting one would make this criterion and C-001 unachievable for any mission that legitimately adds a precondition wait, which pressures the next author to avoid the rule rather than disclose under it. What the scan now guarantees is that new budgets are VISIBLE and individually accounted for here; before this repair, four were invisible.

criteria.evidence: Band REBUILT at closeout after the pre-merge squad's evidence lens showed the previous replacement was selection-biased: it stated the method 'every CI Quality run on the train before the base whose playwright job succeeded', but re-running that method yields 109 qualifying runs and the ten shipped were ranks 94-109 -- the slowest tail, with 93 qualifying runs below the claimed floor. Two real defects were under it. (1) The suite GREW 1229 -> 2777 tests across the window and duration tracks test count, so 'every run' mixes incomparable work; the honest, checkable filter is passed >= 2600 (within 6.4% of the closeout's 2777), which adds 34629381528 and 34665531460 and removes 34606532461 (only 2324 tests). (2) The INSTRUMENT was mixed: 25.6 -- the figure the original NFR-004 was written against -- is Playwright's SUITE SELF-TIME (`2777 passed (25.6m)` in run 34820757579), while 26.85 is that run's JOB WALL-CLOCK. Two instruments, not the 'unreconciled discrepancy' an earlier revision recorded. CURRENT BASIS -- suite self-time, n=11: 34650920361 16.5, 34777305434 18.7, 34632185898 22.7, 34657971585 23.1, 34629381528 23.8, 34660223036 24.2, 34767078079 24.3, 34637284298 24.3, 34673156155 24.6, 34665531460 24.9, 34820757579 25.6. Band 16.5-25.6 min, spread 55.2% on comparable work with no code change. FINAL READING: 16.8 min suite self-time (run 35375268744 @ afe7be3c, `2777 passed (16.8m)`, identical 2777/147 test shape) -- INSIDE the band. CORROBORATION, and it is what settles the retraction: a SECOND closeout run on effectively identical code reads 19.5 min suite self-time (run 35381688538 @ d4dc70d0, `2776 passed (19.5m)`, job wall-clock 20.87 min). Two readings on the same code and the same instrument, 2.7 min apart, both INSIDE the 16.5-25.6 band. That is direct evidence that the earlier 'the suite got faster' narrative was reading run-to-run variance -- the same variance the 55.2% band spread already described -- rather than an effect of the fixes. No mechanism needed explaining because there was no effect to explain.
criteria.notes: The original NFR-004 ('within 5% of 25.6 min') would have fired on EIGHT of these eleven unmodified pre-mission runs. An earlier revision of this row said 'six of ten', which was both computed on the biased set and INVERTED -- it stated the pass count as the fire count. Corrected by the squad's evidence lens. RETRACTED with it: the claim that the closeout reading was OUTSIDE the band and the retry-cost explanation built on top of it. Both were artifacts of comparing job wall-clock (17.93) against a band anchored on a self-time figure. On one instrument there is no anomaly to explain: 16.8 sits just inside a 16.5-25.6 band. The retry explanation was independently falsified anyway -- 34820757579 and the closeout run both report 1 flaky and an identical 2777 passed / 147 skipped, so retry cost cannot account for the difference between them. Also retracted: 'pre-mission runs carried 1-3 flaky each' (34606532461 carried 5, and counts vary BETWEEN runs of identical code -- 35375268744 reports 1, 35381688538 reports 2 -- so no single number characterises a run. (An earlier revision claimed one run printed 1, 2 AND 3; that was this mission's own commit message being echoed by the lint-code job and grepped back as if it were test output. Corrected by the squad's evidence lens.)) and 'two of the flakes were mission items' (that run's five include items 6, 9 and 10).

criteria.description: Zero failures in the final pre-merge run
criteria.evidence: Run 35374639239 @ 38d2b145 and run 35375265259 @ afe7be3c, webkit, --retries=0, selectors verified to resolve before each invocation: 140+60 = 200 executions each, ALL TWELVE ITEMS 10/10, zero failures. PRECISION on the afe7be3c sample, corrected by the squad's evidence lens: run 35375265259 was RE-RUN, so it has two attempts. ATTEMPT 1 showed 199/200, the single failure being `page.goto: WebKit encountered an internal error` -- a browser-level fault, not an assertion failure. ATTEMPT 2 showed 200/200. The GitHub UI surfaces only the latest attempt, so a reviewer opening that run id sees `success` and no trace of the fault; attempt 1 is reachable via the attempts API. Calling it an 'immediate resample' was imprecise -- it is the same run id re-run, not a second run. The fault is absent from the four prior rig runs (~960 executions) and from 35379093636. Recorded rather than discarded; tracked in issue #456. Earlier at e150b8f9, run 35371247321 gave 360/360 across three sections including both experiment arms. PROVENANCE (squad finding D2): run 35371247321 was taken at e150b8f9, whose cure -- a hand-rolled waitForFunction frame counter -- was REPLACED at f1c9cc5c after the correctness and architecture lenses falsified it, and the experiment arms were removed in the same round. So its 360/360 (and any --workers=1 arm figure) describes a SUPERSEDED cure and no post-f1c9cc5c arm reading exists; none is claimed. The SHIPPED cure is carried by 200-execution runs at the harder workers:2 condition: 35374639239 @ 38d2b145, 35375265259 @ afe7be3c, and 35379093636 (its SHA c591764a was orphaned by the commitlint reword; cite the run id, per this mission's own rule), each 140+60 = 200 passed / 0 failed with all selectors verified. PRECISION on how those runs reach the tip, because an earlier revision of this caveat said 'a byte-identical spec file' and that premise expired one commit after it was written (squad finding N2, the same shape as D2 recurring): since f1c9cc5c the only spec change is sk-team-overview-shell-layout.spec.ts, and its only EXECUTABLE delta is adding `.catch(() => false)` to the waitForTimeout arm of the fonts race. Everything else is comment. A catch on a raced timer can suppress an unhandled teardown rejection; it cannot make a failing test pass, so the three runs remain evidence about the shipped behaviour. The precondition wait itself is byte-identical to what the root-cause lens cleared. MEASURED AT THE MERGE CANDIDATE (squad findings R1-CL1 / R2-C1 / R3-4c / R4-N9, raised by all four lenses): three rig runs on the shipped tree, the last at the merge candidate itself -- 35385065116 @ d2799ed6, 35385502326 @ aaebf8db and 35388602800 @ b66a7d3d -- each printing 'Selectors: all 11 line-items resolved from their titleAnchors -- 1:425 2:496 3:512 4:537 5:582 6:154 7:210 8:353 9:495 10:654 11:1113' then 140+60 = 200 passed / 0 failed at --retries=0 with workers inherited (2 under CI, the harder condition). `git diff d2799ed6 b66a7d3d -- apps/storybook/src/tests/` is empty, so all three measure the same tree. This supersedes the inference below rather than resting on it: the earlier rows bridged to the tip by arguing a `.catch` on a raced timer cannot turn a red green, which is true but unnecessary now that the measurement exists. The printed Selectors line is itself the artifact proving the resolver tracks edits rather than storing stale integers.
criteria.notes: PASSES, and the SCOPE of the claim is stated so it cannot be read wider than it is: 'zero failures' means the mission's twelve canonical items under webkit at --retries=0, measured by the repeat rig. It does NOT mean the whole playwright job is flake-free. The closeout CI run 35375268744 is fully green (every job success or skipped, gate: success) but still reports 1 flaky test -- `sk-notice-forced-colors.spec.ts:121` under webkit -- which was never in this mission's scope. Pre-mission runs carried flaky tests tests each, and the population is broader than these twelve items; two of the pre-mission flakes WERE mission items and are fixed. The remainder is enumerated with run ids in issue #456 so that #453 closing cannot be read as 'the webkit lane is de-flaked'. Root cause of the twelve: a test-measurement defect (items 1/4) and a story-render race (items 6-9), neither the originally hypothesised cause.

negative_invariants.description: The rig's file:line selectors resolve to their intended tests in the composed tree
negative_invariants.verification_method: node scripts/webkit-repeat-run.mjs -- resolves every line-item from its titleAnchor and refuses on 0 or 2+ matches
negative_invariants.evidence: The rig no longer STORES a line number at all -- it RESOLVES each item's line at run time from a per-item `titleAnchor`, requiring that anchor to match exactly one `test(` declaration in its file. Zero matches (renamed or deleted test) and two or more (an anchor that cannot identify one test) both refuse. This replaced a guard that merely DETECTED drift against stored integers, after that guard caught a seventh drift -- introduced by this mission's own squad-fix commit, which added 18 comment lines above four anchors. Detection is not prevention when the thing detected is caused by ordinary correct edits to the file above. Proved both ways: injecting 25 comment lines above the tests, the resolver TRACKS them (6:179 7:235 8:378 9:520); renaming a test so its anchor vanishes, it REFUSES with 'matches 0 test( declarations' instead of selecting a neighbour. At head all eleven resolve, and a squad lens re-ran a same-file cross-matrix: 32 cross-pairs, 0 false passes, down from 12 under the previous 'any 4+ character label word' rule.
